clusters.title: In loads_factored and the beam fills, one load kind is missing, doubled, mixed in unit, or bound to the wrong number, and the 'factored' / 'service' basis that was read never holds the answer
clusters.root_cause: [load-reading-factored-and-beam] (i) The findLoads word rule (reader.js 267-270) has the gap [^0-9.;=]{0,28}?, which lets a label with no number of its own ('no dead load,', 'dead load is negligible,', 'no live load,') take the next load's number. The 2 klf is then used as both dead and live load (187/129/188). (ii) FILL.loads_factored (2505-2516) keeps the first D and the first L, takes the unit of the first load, and asks only when NEITHER kind was read. It computes loadBasis() at 2508 and never uses it. So: 'L = 2D', 'D = L = 20 k' and 'dead and live loads 20 k each' silently drop one kind (03, 04). A second dead load with the same value is hidden, because the unit field quotes the same words (05). plf is mixed with k/ft (07). 'factored dead load D = 30 k' has two readings (01), and 'service load D, L' asks for D + L (02), yet both still print 1.2D + 1.6L. (iii) The findLoads symbol rule at 236 reads 'Pu = 1.2D + 1.6L' as Pu = 1: N backtracks from 1.2 to 1, and '.' then passes the (?![A-Za-z0-9]) lookahead (06). (iv) beamAnalysisFields 2186-2189 raises loads_basis as a 'choice' on boxes it has already filled. mergeBoxes only attaches that as a ruleQuestion, and markReaderStops ignores it, so the factored loads are factored again (65). loadBasis 1426 needs a digit right after 'factored loads:', so 'factored loads: wD = 1.2' is read as service-symbol (150).
clusters.fix_plan: [load-reading-factored-and-beam] Same lane as L2 (load-pair-half-missing + load-number-misbound): extend those hunks, do not build a second load reader. (1) Put L2's half-missing ask (kind 'need') into FILL.loads_factored as well (after 2513) and into beamAnalysisFields for wD/wL (after 2185). Skip it when the missing kind is negated in its own clause (no|zero|none|negligible|neglect(ed)|= 0); then the box stays empty, which is right. With L2(c)'s gap fix this gives ANSWER 160 (187, 129) and 120 (188, with fix-hercombo). (2) L2(3)'s coverage patterns must also accept the no-verb form 'dead and live loads 20 k each' and 'D = L = 20 k' (04: 56). 'L = 2D', 'D = L', 'half the live load', 'L/D = 3' are relations: ASK. fix-hercombo already stops 03 itself, but not its D = L / L = 30 k, D = L variants. (3) FILL.loads_factored: two loads of the same kind at different positions (compare by index, not by value) raise an ASK, kind 'need', on D (or L) asking for the total; never keep the first silently (05). When d.unit and l.unit differ: klf with plf, convert plf/1000 and print k/ft (ANSWER 2.72 for 07); kips with lb, or psf with k/ft, ASK. (4) Use the computed basis. basis 'factored' from the words 'factored dead|live load' with no u-load: ASK, kind 'need' (01: a given factored value, or the asked 1.2D). Explicit service|working|unfactored, with the words never saying factored/Pu/wu/U: STOP in one sentence, no number ('the page works out factored loads; your question asks for the service load') (02). (5) L2(a): the unitless branch at 236 must reject the WHOLE numeric token when it is followed by a letter or '(': test the text after the full token for ^[\d.]*\s*[A-Za-z(*+]. L2's planned \s*[(*x+] misses '1.2D' because N backtracks to '1'. 06 then reads D = 20, L = 30 and prints 72. (6) beamAnalysisFields 2189: when the loads are said to be factored, do not fill wD/wL. If both are individually labelled factored (findLoads basis 'factored'), set already_factored and w_u = X + Y (ANSWER 220 for 65; the sum of two factored loads is wu, unambiguous). Otherwise ASK, kind 'need', on w_u. loadBasis givenFactored should also match 'factored\s+loads?\s*[:,]?\s*[A-Za-z]{1,3}\s*=' (L2(f), add ':'), so 150 asks. MUST NOT CHANGE: L2's list; 'dead load = 0' and 'dead load neglected' after the live load (already right); dead-load-only questions with no live word (hercombo/dcauses); the 'dead + live = 120 psf is a sum' guard; a given 'Pu = 800 kips'; C-28's framing weight.

clusters.title: With no blank, a sentence asks for a different moment or load than the form prints (nominal Mn, plastic Mp, extra moment, unfactored or dead-load moment, ML, the moment at a point, a named 1.4D, the total load on a beam, wu in plf / as a line load), and the form's Mu / phi Mp / U stays a clean ANSWER + A sentence that asks for the NOMINAL value (Fcr, Pn, Mn, 'nominal axial strength', '(not phi Pn)') or the ASD value (Pn/omega, Fcr/omega, 'allowable strength') gets the form's phi (LRFD design) value as a clean ANSWER
clusters.root_cause:
[prose-asked-quantity-beams-loads] pipeline.js ASK_WORDS / askedInWords (975-1035) know only the forms' main quantities. The qualifiers that change the quantity exist only on the blank path (wordId 922). 'nominal moment strength' matches phimn (989), the form's own result, so nothing is flagged. 'plastic moment', 'moment at the quarter point', 'moment due to dead load only' and 'ML' match nothing. 'unfactored moment' fails the mu entry, because 'unfactored' has no word boundary before 'factored'. asksInProse (1002) does not count 'how much' as asking. 'what is Mu for the load combination 1.4D' asks mu and gets the 1.2D + 1.6L carry (the chain's combo_first, ~3245). 'total factored load on the beam (in kips)' matches pu (993), which FORM_GIVES.floor_plan (817) claims to give, so the beam reaction stands as the answer. The asked unit is never compared with the printed one: SIG_VALUE.wu accepts loads_combinations' U_max in psf (loads-09: 32 psf printed for a k/ft line load), and a prose 'wu in plf' never reaches sigValueFor's klf-to-plf conversion (1240; the writeBlock unit check at 3809-3814 covers only kip-in vs kip-ft).
[nominal-asd-sentence] pipeline.js: the nominal conversion (SIG_NOMINAL l.846, sigValue l.1096) and the 'nominal|allowable|asd|omega' guard (wordId l.922) are reached only through askedBlanks, that is, a typed 'Sym = ____'. On the sentence path: asksInProse (l.1002) needs an asking verb, so a question typed as a bare head phrase ('Pn for a W10x49 ...', 'Fcr for KL/r = 85 ...', 'nominal axial strength of ...', 'allowable strength of ...') asks nothing. ASK_WORDS (l.975-999) has no bare Fcr / Pn / Mn / nominal entry, and its phipn / phifcr entries match 'phi Pn' inside '(not phi Pn)'. writeBlock's STRENGTH_ASK (l.1038) keeps the form's ANSWER whenever 'strength' is in the text. This is the same root as lane L3 prose-asks [prose-ask-qualifier]. That plan covers 'nominal' / bare 'Pn' -> pn and 'allowable|ASD|omega' -> STOP, but only for sentences its asking test accepts. It does not name Fcr, Mn/Mp, '(not phi X)', or verb-less head phrases that contain digits.
clusters.fix_plan:
[prose-asked-quantity-beams-loads] Build on L3's prose-ask helper (a new file called at the end of askedInWords); do not build a second one. Add to its qualifier list, for moments and loads: (a) 'nominal (moment|flexural) strength', \bMn\b(?!\s*=), 'plastic moment', \bMp\b(?!\s*=) with no phi give id 'mp' (it already exists on the blank route, in sigGives): ANSWER Mp = Fy Zx/12, 558.33 (106) and 138.33 (107). That is unambiguous for her fully braced beams. Exclude 'nominal' before the phimn match. (b) extra|additional|excess|reserve|spare|remaining + moment|capacity|load, with 'how much' counted as asking: UNKNOWN ask, so CHECK YOUR BLANK stands under the ANSWER (110). (c) unfactored|service|working + moment|load, 'moment due to (the) dead|live load (only)', \bM[DL]\b: UNKNOWN ask, CHECK (189, 131, 133). Also fix the mu entry so 'unfactored' never counts as 'factored'. (d) 'moment at <position>' where the position is not midspan, center or 'maximum' (quarter point, 'N ft from', x = N with N not L/2): UNKNOWN ask, CHECK (128, 125). (e) A load combination named in the asking sentence other than 1.2D + 1.6L ('1.4D', '0.9D', 'combination 1') gives a STOP in one sentence with no number: her class uses one combination (127). Coordinate with fix-hercombo. (f) 'total (factored) load on the beam|girder|joist' or 'W = wu L' is not pu (pu stays for column/axial/'on the column'): an UNKNOWN ask, so floor_plan's reaction line is no longer clean (loads-12). (g) Asked unit: when the asking sentence names a unit (in plf|lb/ft|klf|k/ft|kips|psf), compare its dimension with the printed value. Same dimension, other scale (plf vs k/ft): write the existing sigValueFor conversion as an 'ANSWER TO "wu in plf"' line with one number and demote the main line to ALSO FOUND (loads-14). A wu / 'line load' ask, or a spacing/tributary in the words, answered by a psf U_max: askedMismatch, the existing NOT WHAT YOUR BLANK ASKS line or a STOP (loads-09). Routing roof live as L to loads_floor (her rule) is optional coverage, only after regress. MUST NOT CHANGE: L3's list; 'find Mu', 'maximum moment', 'design moment strength phi Mn' (the form's own result); 'moment at midspan' of a simple uniform beam (= Mmax); the whole blank path; 'factored load on the column' = pu; word questions and multiple choice (C-48); the one-number ANSWER line (altnum).
[nominal-asd-sentence] Hand these 9 hits to the prose-asks fixer as extra test cases, plus this delta in the same new helper file. Do not add a second mechanism. (1) Asking test: the part's FIRST clause counts as asking even with digits and no verb when it STARTS with a quantity name followed by for|of ('Pn for a W10x49', 'Fcr for KL/r = 85', 'nominal axial strength of', 'allowable strength of', 'effective net area of'). (2) Before the ASK_WORDS phi entries match, strip '(not phi X)' / 'not phi X' / 'rather than phi X' / 'instead of phi X', and record that the sentence asks the NOMINAL X. (3) Map bare 'Fcr' (no phi in front), 'nominal (critical|buckling) stress' -> fcr; 'Mn', 'nominal moment (strength)' -> mn; 'Mp' / 'plastic moment' -> mp; bare 'Pn', 'nominal (axial|compressive) strength' -> pn. The existing SIG_NOMINAL / 'mp' sigValue then prints ANSWER TO '...': Fcr = 26.5/0.90 = 29.4 (look-20/21), Pn = 523 (look-22/23/24), Mp = Fy Zx/12 = 420.8 (look-25), and the phi line becomes ALSO FOUND. Unambiguous: one phi each. (4) 'omega' / '/ omega' / 'ASD' / 'allowable (strength|stress|load)' on column, Fcr or beam forms: one-sentence STOP with no number ('her class is LRFD; the page gives design values phi Pn, not ASD values. NOT answered here'). This covers look-26/27/28, which STRENGTH_ASK otherwise keeps clean. MUST NOT CHANGE: 'phi Fcr for KL/r = 85' and Table 4-14 lookups, 'design strength', 'available strength' (LRFD), her review 'Find: Euler Pcr, the AISC phi Pn', 'Pn = ____' blanks (already right), 'Fy = 50' given values, 'maximum allowable load' max-load questions (lane max-load-ask-unrouted owns them).

clusters.title: Column bracing: 'unbraced' / 'no bracing at mid height' read as a brace, a brace about the x axis put on y, and a brace sentence with no location ignored + A takedown's floor count in 'the roof and three levels' or '4-story' is not read, and the floors box silently defaults to 0 (the roof alone is printed)
clusters.root_cause:
[column-bracing-addons] reader.js findBracing (1844-1856). Line 1846 has no \b before 'braced', so 'unbraced at mid height' matches, and no negation check ('no bracing at mid height', 'bracing at mid height: none', 'the brace ... has been removed'). It records no axis ('about the x axis', 'strong axis only'), and fillColumn (1943-1952) always puts the fraction on Ly. A brace statement with no location word ('(c) what if braced about both axes') is not read as a brace at all (it needs mid/third/quarter). bothDir needs Ls.brace.fraction, the stem's 20 ft fills both lengths, and (c) silently prints (a)'s 399 again.
[takedown-floor-count] The floorsN regex (reader.js 747-753) needs '<n>\s+(floor|story|storey)', so 'three levels', '4-story' and 'four-story' are not read. FILL.loads_takedown 2482 asks for 'floors' with no kind, so the frozen engine default 0 goes in (pipeline mergeBoxes 549, state 'default'). The page prints the roof alone, 22.4 for 233.6, as a clean ANSWER; only the read box says the floor loads were not used.
clusters.fix_plan:
[column-bracing-addons] Same lane as L2 [column-bracing-reading] (a) negation and (b) axis; do not plan it twice. Additions for that lane: a \b before 'braced' and the 'un' prefix (15: 399); a negation AFTER the match counts too (': none', 'none', 'is not provided'; variant 163); the axis words 'x axis', 'x-x', 'strong axis', 'strong direction' and 'weak axis is not' (151: 399.2). New: a brace statement with no location word (braced about or in both axes/directions, braced about the weak axis), in a part whose own text gives no mid/third/quarter/height, raises an ASK kind 'need' on Ly/Lx ('where along the column is the brace?'). Never the unbraced answer (140 (c)). MUST NOT CHANGE: L2's list (plain 'braced at mid-height', 'in both directions', 'braced against sidesway', HW 5-17 segments, the 9/9 third-point column).
[takedown-floor-count] Same lane as L2 [takedown-floors-and-levels] (a)/(b); do not plan twice. Additions: (1) Safety: line 2482 asks with kind 'need' whenever floor loads (floor_D_psf / floor_L_psf) were read. Never the default 0 with floor loads in the words; this also covers a text with no count at all (ASK). (2) Coverage: the count regex also accepts a hyphen ('4-story', 'four-story'), and '(the )?roof and (WN) (levels|floors)' gives floors = N below the roof. That is unambiguous: ANSWER 233.6. A bare 'N levels' or 'N-story building' with roof loads keeps L2(b)'s ASK. MUST NOT CHANGE: L2's list; a roof-only column ('supports only the roof') stays at 0 floors with no ask.

clusters.title: Numbered problems on one line are not split, a later numbered part borrows an earlier column's length, and a leading problem number is read as a count
clusters.root_cause: [numbered-problems-and-labels] (i) A second numbered problem on the same line ('... find phi pn. 2. a pl 1/2x8 ...', 'q1 ... q2 ...') is not split. pipeline.js splitAsks (646-671) counts an ask only when its verb opens a clause (ASK_VERB_RE 592), and the frozen finder does not take a mid-line '2.' or 'q2' as a part marker. The single part then mixes both problems: tensionCommon (reader 1582) takes the W as the member and ignores the PL (702), and findGrade takes q2's a36 for q1's column (368.6). (ii) carryAcross section 3 (pipeline ~3483) fills a later part's empty lengths, ends and Fy from an earlier column part, even when the later part names a DIFFERENT shape and says nothing like 'repeat' or 'same'. 471 is printed for a W10x49 whose length is not given, and the block does not say the length was borrowed. (iii) reader.js cgTokens (854/863): a leading 'N.' followed by a lower-case word is not a STOP or a label, so in '5. bolts per line: 3' the 5 becomes the count and the 'count LAST' rule never reads ': 3'.
clusters.fix_plan: [numbered-problems-and-labels] (1) pipeline (a new file, or splitAsks): when the finder made ONE part of a text that has a problem marker after a sentence end or at a clause start, (?:^|[.?!;]\s*)(?:q\s?\d{1,2}\b|problem\s+\d+\b|\d{1,2}\s*[.)]\s+), and its own member shape on each side (two different members), STOP in one sentence with no number: 'Your text holds two numbered problems; type them one at a time.' (67, 147). Real splitting is optional coverage, after regress. (2) carryAcross section 3: skip the carry when the target part names a shape that differs from the source part's shape, unless the part says repeat|same|again|also|as in. Its length box then stays empty and required, so the page asks (146: ASK). (3) cgTokens: an integer at the start of the text or after a sentence end, followed by '.' or ')' and a space, is a label when the count phrase it would fill gets its own number after ':' or '='. That gives ANSWER 96.9 for 148 (596.2 / 129.6 for its variants). When no other number fills that count, go through the existing count_ conflict ask ('can be read two ways'); never use the label as a count (variant 216). MUST NOT CHANGE: lettered (a)/(b) parts and their carry from the stem; 'repeat (a) for a W10x49' (REF_RE); 'q4.', '4)', 'problem 4.', '4. given:' (already right); his own '(a) ... (b)' sample; a plain '3 bolts per line'.

clusters.title: An asked area is not the printed one: 'effective net area' in a no-holes run prints phi Pn (even a typed 'Ae = ____' gets no warning), 'net area' with no hole words prints An = Ag (holes taken as zero), 'area ... minus two 1 in holes' prints the gross area
clusters.root_cause: [asked-area-not-given] (a) pipeline.js askedLines l.1515 'v = sigValueFor(...); if (!v) continue;' silently drops an asked quantity that the form gives in general (sigGives > 0) but this run does not hold. In no-holes mode tension_capacity has no Ae value, so no line, no demotion and no warning appear. I checked on the branch: 'effective net area of a w14x90 Ae = ____ in2' prints the phi Pn ANSWER with nothing under it. The verb-less prose 'effective net area of a w14x90 no holes' is not even an ask (asksInProse needs a verb). (b) reader.js tensionCommon l.1649: the holes_count ask has the default kind 'value', which does not block, so tension_net_area runs with zero holes when the words name none ('net area of a w14x90' -> An = Ag). A count that is not in the words becomes 0. (c) The frozen finder routes 'area of a w14x90 minus two 1 in holes' to lookup_shape, and FILL.lookup_shape (l.2531) never looks at hole words.
clusters.fix_plan: [asked-area-not-given] (1) pipeline.js askedLines l.1515 (a 2-3 line hunk): when !v and sigGives(lastFn, b.id) > 0, set part.askedMissing = b. writeBlock then uses the EXISTING askedMismatch path: a 'NOT WHAT YOUR BLANK ASKS' line, and the ANSWER is demoted. For a typed blank, always. For a prose ask, only when it is the part's only ask. This must be the SAME hunk as lane L3 form-choice-guards (a), which handles 'gives none of the asks'; this is 'gives it in general, not in this run'. The verb-less head phrase comes from the prose-asks delta (cluster nominal-asd-sentence). (2) reader.js tensionCommon: for fn tension_net_area with NO hole/bolt/rivet/welded/'no holes' word, raise holes_count with kind 'need'. This is one more condition on lane L1's kind change (tension-holes-unread-nonblocking), so look-56 ASKs 'How many holes ... in each flange, and in the web?'. (3) reader.js FILL.lookup_shape: hole words with a count, or minus|less|deduct|subtract|net + holes, give a STOP with no number ('your question takes holes out of the area: that is the net area, not the shape's area; NOT answered as a look-up'). Never the gross area (look-57). Two elements are possible (flange 25.08 / web 25.62), so no ANSWER. MUST NOT CHANGE: 'net area of a w14x90 with no holes' (An = Ag, said in words), welded members, tension_capacity with holes printing Ae, 'Ag = ____' of a capacity question, 'A of a W14x90', 'find the net area ... (2 holes per flange)' runs.
